items.claim: Prov.10.9 is correctly isolated from Prov.10.8 and Prov.10.10, but the row's own quoted form for the verse's second colon silently drops a real prefix letter carried by the source word.
items.evidence: Prov.10.9's own boundary claim holds: consonantal_index shows zero shared content tokens between Prov.10.8/Prov.10.9 and Prov.10.9/Prov.10.10, and Prov.10.8 and Prov.10.10 both close on the byte-identical line "וֶאֱוִ֥יל שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט" (oshb:Prov.10.8) / "וֶאֱוִ֥יל שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט" (oshb:Prov.10.10), which Prov.10.9 does not repeat. But the row quotes the verse's second colon as bare "מעקש דרכיו", while the actual pointed word at that position is "וּמְעַקֵּ֥שׁ" (oshb:Prov.10.9) -- a vav-conjunctive prefix the row's quote omits. A naive skeleton check passes this quote only because "מעקש" is a contiguous substring of "ומעקש"; a word-bound check shows no standalone token matching the row's bare form. The quote is also unpointed throughout and its tier is never disclosed in the row.
tier_citations: skeleton (row quote, substring-only match -- masks a dropped vav prefix)

items.claim: The cluster's catchword evidence is byte-verified correct, but the device_notes claim that Prov.10.16-17 both lack an adversative “but” misdescribes Prov.10.17's own WEB rendering.
items.evidence: Re-running the sweep independently (word-bound, exact spelling) confirms the row's core claim exactly: the prefixed noun matching oshb:Prov.10.16/oshb:Prov.10.17 occurs in exactly 4 verses book-wide (Prov.10.16, Prov.10.17, Prov.11.19, Prov.19.23), and Prov.10.16-Prov.10.17 is the only adjacent pair among them; the excluded neighbors Prov.10.15 and Prov.10.18 carry zero shared skeleton content tokens with the span. However, device_notes states 'Both cola are synthetic (no adversative “but”)', while WEB's own rendering of the second verse reads: “He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others astray.” (web:Prov.10.17) -- which contains 'but'. The Hebrew itself carries only a plain vav on the second clause (ambiguous and/but), so the parenthetical claim is not supportable by appeal to either witness as stated.
tier_citations: skeleton (sweep, correctly disclosed as such by the row)
WEB (verbatim, web:Prov.10.17, contradicts the row's parenthetical)

items.claim: Prov.10.18's isolation from Prov.10.17 and Prov.10.19 is byte-confirmed, but the row's quoted form for the verse's second speech-sin again drops a real prefix letter present in the source word.
items.evidence: Consonantal_index confirms zero shared content tokens on both of the row's claimed boundaries (Prov.10.17/Prov.10.18 and Prov.10.18/Prov.10.19), supporting the single_proverb call. But the row quotes "מוצא דבה" for the verse's second speech-sin, while the actual pointed word at that position is "וּמוֹצִ֥א" (oshb:Prov.10.18) -- again a dropped vav-conjunctive, matching only as a substring at skeleton tier rather than as a word-bound token, the same prefix-extension pattern found in another row of this same span. The quote is unpointed and its tier is undisclosed.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that Prov.10.20 "finds no lexical echo" with Prov.10.21 "in either neighbor's own imagery" is contradicted by two shared skeleton tokens the row does not disclose.
items.evidence: Consonantal_index shows Prov.10.20 and Prov.10.21 share the word-bound tokens "לב" (heart: oshb:Prov.10.20 "לֵ֖ב", oshb:Prov.10.21 "לֵ֥ב") and "צדיק" (righteous: oshb:Prov.10.20 "צַדִּ֑יק", oshb:Prov.10.21 "צַ֭דִּיק") -- an undisclosed cross-seam continuity straddling the row's own boundary with its immediate neighbor. Both verses build their contrast on a righteous body-part-of-speech image paired with a statement about lev, which the row's rejected_alternative flatly denies sharing. This does not overturn the single_proverb call -- book-wide word-bound sweeps put this exact tsadiq form at 34 verses and this exact lev form at 47 verses, so the overlap is chapter-generic vocabulary rather than a distinctive two-verse catchword -- but the absolute 'no lexical echo' claim is factually wrong and undisclosed.
tier_citations: skeleton (word-bound sweep counts: tsadiq 34 verses book-wide, lev 47 verses book-wide)

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that Prov.10.25's "storm imagery has nothing in common" with Prov.10.24 is contradicted by a shared skeleton token, and the row's own quote drops a real prefix letter from the source.
items.evidence: Prov.10.24 and Prov.10.25 share the word-bound token "רשע" (wicked: oshb:Prov.10.24 "רָ֭שָׁע", oshb:Prov.10.25 "רָשָׁ֑ע"), so the rejected_alternative's absolute 'nothing in common' is not accurate as stated, though this exact form sweeps to 36 verses book-wide and is chapter-generic antithetic vocabulary, not a distinguishing catchword, so the single_proverb call itself is not threatened. Separately, the row quotes "תאות צדיקים" for the verse's second colon, while the actual pointed word is "וְתַאֲוַ֖ת" (oshb:Prov.10.24) -- the same dropped-vav-conjunctive pattern found elsewhere in this span, matching the row's bare form only as a skeleton substring, not a word-bound token.
tier_citations: skeleton (row quote, substring-only match; sweep count 36 verses book-wide for the shared term)
